clue.text: Group of scouts to prepare for trip

definitions.meaning: a troop of young Cub Scouts is called by this name
to fill a suitcase before travelling

explanation.surface: Scout leaders getting the troop ready for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a unit of Cub Scouts, and the act of putting belongings in luggage before a journey.

clue.text: Dismiss up-and-coming bands

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bands are hoops, and the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at promising new music groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-and-coming' looks like praise for new groups, but in a down entry it says read upwards: two HOOPs written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff at something is to brush it aside contemptuously, a dismissal.

clue.text: Mention current measures introduced in holiday area

indicators.note: one thing introduced in another is placed inside it

parts.note: to mention is to cite
amps are units measuring electric current

explanation.surface: Talk of electrical safety standards being brought into a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where people pitch tents on holiday is a holiday area.

clue.text: Old man rushed round building and dropped

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for one's father, an old man

indicators.note: rushed is wrapped round the building, enclosing it

parts.note: rushed means raced
a hut is a simple building

explanation.surface: An elderly father dashing around a building before falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivered by canopy from an aircraft, so dropped from the sky.

clue.text: Wartime refuge near North Leeds demolished about end of forties

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed about the extra letter, enclosing it
something demolished is knocked down and rebuilt, so these letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An air-raid shelter close to a Yorkshire city knocked down in the late 1940s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges NEAR NORTH LEEDS, and 'about' puts that around S, the last letter of 'forties' given by 'end of'. An ANDERSON SHELTER was a corrugated-iron garden air-raid shelter in Second World War Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A backyard bunker against air raids in the Second World War, a refuge for wartime families.

clue.text: Book, a long one penned in support of cleric leading church

indicators.note: the cleric comes first, leading the church abbreviation

parts.note: a year is a long stretch of time
pro means in favour of, giving support
Ven is the abbreviation of Venerable, a title for an archdeacon
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lengthy volume written in defence of a priest who heads a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' is a link that suits the book of the surface. A YEAR IN PROVENCE is Peter Mayle's memoir of life in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestselling travel memoir, so a published volume.

clue.text: Husband lifted handle, type

indicators.note: in a down entry lifted means raised, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A husband raising a door handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a door fitting; it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscular macho man is a recognisable type of person.

clue.text: Nevertheless, piled up soil conceals one burial place

parts.note: tho is a short form of though, meaning nevertheless

indicators.note: conceals means the one is put out of sight, taken away from the word
in a down entry piled up means stacked upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Yet a heap of earth hides a single body in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piled up' turns SOIL into LIOS, and 'conceals' removes I (one) to leave LOS. A THOLOS is an ancient Greek beehive-shaped tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient domed tomb is a place where the dead were buried.

clue.text: Courting is going out of fashion

definitions.meaning: becoming old-fashioned or out of date

explanation.surface: Romance is no longer the trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: romantic seeing of a partner, and becoming passé as time leaves a thing behind.

clue.text: Change refunded, having missed several courses?

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Getting money back after skipping parts of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests lessons for which a refund is due; it means meal courses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who skipped many courses of a meal has not eaten enough.

clue.text: Empire builder overthrown in part of Asia thus

indicators.note: turned over, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: Nam is short for Vietnam, a country in Asia
thus means so

explanation.surface: A founder of empire toppled in an Asian land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' reads NAM + SO backwards. OSMAN I founded the Ottoman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Ottoman dynasty built a great empire.

clue.text: Good-looking fellow with fancy yacht?

parts.note: a fancy is a dream or daydream
a yacht is a boat

explanation.surface: A handsome man with an expensive sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive man is a heart-throb, a common informal term.

clue.text: Famous Frenchman's former resistance to European Union

indicators.note: resistance is added to the European Union

parts.note: former means past
EU is the European Union
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who once opposed the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'. Louis PASTEUR was the French scientist behind pasteurisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientist who gave his name to heat treatment of milk is a celebrated figure from France.

clue.text: Worn-out piste?

definitions.meaning: a ski slope is a track you go along downhill

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: shabby and exhausted, and humorously a ski track heading downhill.

clue.text: Like jumper who's finished in forbidden territory?

definitions.meaning: a jumper makes bounds; one who has finished is through with jumping
in an area where entry is not allowed

explanation.surface: A showjumper ends up somewhere they should not be.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: done with leaping, punningly, and the idiom for an area that is off limits.

clue.text: Sounds like brother's a proper hedonist

indicators.note: the words are to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: brother is sib, the 's is a link meaning is, a is as written, and proper means right

explanation.surface: A claim that a sibling is a real pleasure-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to luxury and pleasure, after the ancient city of Sybaris.

clue.text: Cheap form of travel always available in coach

indicators.note: always is placed in the coach

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Budget travel being on offer all the time by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a modern bus; it is a STAGE, as in stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest accommodation on a passenger ship was a low-cost way to travel.

clue.text: Title printed in gold on book for decoration

indicators.note: the title is printed in the middle, placed inside the other letters
in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Gilt lettering on a book cover makes it decorative.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is an object used for adorning, a decoration.

clue.text: Supplier of engine device

definitions.meaning: a firm that supplies goods to retailers
the part of a petrol engine that sends current to the spark plugs

explanation.surface: A firm that sells engine parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a wholesaler that delivers goods, and the part routing ignition current in a car motor.

clue.text: Wild animal beginning to pose big problem

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, big
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A wild creature starting to cause a major difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial of Australia and America living in the wild.

clue.text: Former students engulfed in calumnies

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed up inside the following word

explanation.surface: Ex-students caught up in a slander scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates of a school or college are its former students.

clue.text: Enjoying holiday — a novel trip to Spain

indicators.note: Spain is added to the end
a trip is a stumble, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A vacation spent reading a book on a trip to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the anagram signal; it is fodder, and 'trip' rearranges A NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away from work or duty on permitted absence is enjoying a holiday.

clue.text: Patrollers regularly seen in city abroad

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Police patrols being seen often in a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Provence, in the south of France, so abroad to a British solver.

clue.text: Crossing Scottish mountain, woman Service supplied by ATS, PO discovered plant

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Crossing Scottish mountain, woman Service supplied by ATS, PO discovered plant': VERA round BEN works, but 'Service supplied by ATS, PO discovered' looks spliced in by OCR, and no scan or search gives the true clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Crossing Scottish mountain, woman Service supplied by ATS, PO discovered plant

clue.text: Heading for scandal, one politician revealed he's a fool

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: A scandal in which an MP is exposed as an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple-minded person is a fool.

clue.text: A little bit hard to leave the old country

indicators.note: the letter for hard leaves, taken out of the word

parts.note: Thrace is an ancient country of south-east Europe
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is somewhat difficult to emigrate from one's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old country' suggests emigrants' homeland; it is THRACE, the ancient region by the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, as in a trace of salt.

clue.text: Road in US terminates unexpectedly

indicators.note: the letters fall into an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: An American road comes to a sudden end.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal shopping road of an American town is so called.

clue.text: Pressure in part of contest

definitions.meaning: as in the ... being on, stress
a preliminary round of a race

explanation.surface: Feeling the strain during a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: intense strain, and a qualifying round in a competition.
